claim: Hot 100 peaks: Got to Be There 4, Rockin' Robin 2, I Wanna Be Where You Are 16, Ben 1, With a Child's Heart 50, We're Almost There 54, Just a Little Bit of You 23, Don't Stop 1, Rock with You 1, Off the Wall 10, She's Out of My Life 10 (Apr 1 1980); Ain't No Sunshine UK single only
Billboard 200 peaks: Got to Be There 14 (Jan 24 1972, Gold), Ben 5 (Aug 4 1972), Music & Me 92 (Apr 13 1973), Forever Michael 101 (Jan 16 1975), Off the Wall 3 (Aug 10 1979, RIAA Diamond)
Off the Wall singles: Don't Stop Jul 10 1979, Rock with You Oct 9 1979, Off the Wall Nov 16 1979, She's Out of My Life Apr 1 1980; Rock with You by Rod Temperton

Ben: Walter Scharf and Don Black; theme of the 1972 film Ben, sequel to Willard; Golden Globe for Best Original Song and Oscar nomination; first meant for Donny Osmond, who was touring; recorded at Motown LA in October 1971; Lee Montgomery sings in the film, Jackson's version over end credits; Jackson aged 13
Got to Be There written by Elliot Willensky, launched his solo career, title track of debut solo album, a Top 5 hit
Ben credited music Walter Scharf, lyrics Don Black
Don't Stop: first chart-topper Jackson wrote himself; Quincy Jones encouraged him to write; Greg Phillinganes rhythm arrangement; very high vocal range, overdubbed several times to build harmony
Rockin' Robin: Leon Rene wrote it after a mockingbird pestered him with its singing; Bobby Day original peaked No. 2
First career Grammy at the 22nd Grammy Awards (1980), Best R&B Vocal Performance, Male, for Don't Stop

Off the Wall released Aug 10 1979, fifth solo album, first after leaving Motown for Epic, Quincy Jones producer; first album by a solo artist to spawn four Hot 100 Top 10 hits; Jackson co-produced three tracks including Don't Stop

Rock with You: Rod Temperton, ex-Heatwave keyboardist, flown to LA by Quincy Jones; No. 1 on Jan 19 1980 for four weeks; all four Off the Wall singles reached the Top 10, only Fleetwood Mac had done that before
Off the Wall four Top 10 hits including No. 1s Don't Stop and Rock with You; Diamond certification in the US
Bobby Day original 1958 on Class Records; Leon Rene wrote it as Jimmie Thomas
MusicBrainz search listing: Michael Jackson, Person, born 1958-08-29 Gary; artist page itself not readable (browser check), ID taken from search result
year-end ranks: Ben 20 (1972), Rockin' Robin 41 (1972), Don't Stop 'til You Get Enough 91 (1979)
Ben 1 week at No. 1, week of Oct 14-20 1972; Don't Stop 1 week at No. 1, week of Oct 13-19 1979
